ORAL JUDGMENT : (PER:- Z.A. HAQ, J.)
1] These three petitions are being disposed by common judgment as common point arises for consideration in these petitions.

In these petitions, the challenge is to the validity of Protocol A.18.04 of Appendix B of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (for short "the Rules of 1955") which lays down that "Besan", a product obtained by grinding the dehusked Bengal gram shall not contain any other foreign ingredient or added colouring matter.
The challenge is mainly to the restriction that "Besan" shall not contain any other foreign ingredient.

2] According to the petitioners, Protocol A.18.06.12 permits upto 2% by weight other edible grains in chana dal, and if other edible grains upto 2% are found in Chana Dal, it is not treated as an "adulterated" article of food as defined by Section 2 (ia) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short "the Act of 1954").

The petitioners contend that Protocol A.18.04 of Appendix B of the Rules of 1955, laying down that any other Judgment 6 wp31.09+.odt foreign ingredient is not permissible in "Besan" is arbitrary and illegal inasmuch as if edible grains upto 2% by weight are permitted in Dal Chana,
then to same extent, it should be permitted in "Besan" also as "Besan" is nothing but pulverized form of Dal Chana.

5 the petitioners seek consequential relief of quashing of R.C.C. No. 10/2005 registered against them for the offences punishable under Section 7 (i) read with Sections 2 (ia) (a) and 2 (ia) (m) punishable under Sections 16 (1) (a) (i), 16 (1) (a)
(ii) and 17 (1) (a) (i) and 17 (1) (b) of the Act of 1954 and the Rules of 1955.
3] Learned ASGI and learned advocate appearing for the Food Safety and Standard Authority of India opposed the petitions on the ground that after enforcement of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and repeal of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act 1954, as per Section 97 of the Act of 2006, the challenge in the petitions to Protocol A.18.04 has become infructuous.
4] On merits, it is submitted that edible grains upto 2% by weight are permitted in Dal Chana as the same can be removed by the consumers before its use / consumption, however, in case of "Besan", it being in powder form, such foreign ingredients are not permitted as it is not possible for the consumers to remove the same.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standard Authority of India
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that the protocols are Judgment 7 wp31.09+.odt prepared on recommendation of experts, keeping in view the issues relating to the health of the consumers.

5] After considering the rival submissions, we find that the argument made on behalf of the petitioners that as edible grains upto 2% by weight are permitted in Dal Chana, foreign ingredients to same extent should be permitted in "Besan", cannot be accepted.

The justification given on behalf of the respondents for permitting edible grains upto 2% by weight in Dal Chana and not permitting the same in "Besan" cannot be said to be arbitrary or without any basis.
Hence, we see no reason to accept the challenge made by the petitioners.
6] As we are not inclined to accept the challenge of the petitioners, the other submissions made on behalf of the respondents are not dealt with.
7] In view of the above, the writ petitions are dismissed.
No costs.
8] The petitioners are directed to appear before the trial Court where the prosecutions are pending, on 10/01/2020 at 11:00 am.
9] The trial Court, where the prosecutions are pending is/are directed to expedite the prosecutions and decide the same till 15/04/2020.
